close_reason: Wontfix per JMAP-zx3s.15 counter-research. The workspace canonical pattern (jmap-types::SetResponse: not_created uses HashMap<String, _>) keys creation-id maps by String, not Id. MdnSendRequest.send is correctly HashMap<String, Mdn>; changing to HashMap<Id, Mdn> would lie about the Id contract (URL-safe base64 alphabet, no '#'). The actual divergence was on_success_update_email going to HashMap<Id, _>, which is fixed under .11.
description:
crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mdn.rs:238-258:

```rust
pub struct MdnSendRequest {
    pub account_id: Id,
    pub identity_id: Id,
    pub send: HashMap<String, Mdn>,                              // String key
    pub on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>,  // Id key
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```

`send` keys are client-assigned creation IDs (per RFC 9007 §3.1 / RFC 8620 §5.3). They are referenced from `on_success_update_email` as `'#k1'` (with `#` prefix). The dispatcher resolves them.

`on_success_update_email` uses `HashMap<Id, PatchObject>` (Id-keyed, byte-identical to String on the wire via `#[serde(transparent)]`). The migration test (mdn_send_request_on_success_update_email_roundtrip) explicitly verifies the wire format is identical.

But `send` itself stays `HashMap<String, Mdn>`. Same shape on the wire either way, but the typed-key discipline is inconsistent. A consumer iterating a map of creation IDs gets `&String` here and `&Id` there for the same logical concept.

Fix: change `send` to `HashMap<Id, Mdn>` to match `on_success_update_email` (and to match the pattern that lands in jmap-mail-client's EmailSubmissionSetParams / Mailbox/set etc. for client-assigned creation IDs).

Wire-byte-identical to today (Id is `#[serde(transparent)]` over String). Round-trip test would not change behavior.

Filed as opinion because the wire-format effect is zero. Type-discipline benefit is real but minor — caller ergonomics improve marginally; canonical-template consistency improves more.

Confidence: medium. The Id-keyed pattern is canonical for the workspace but I have not verified that every existing creation-id-keyed map in jmap-mail-types/jmap-chat-types follows the Id-keyed convention. If `HashMap<String, T>` is the prevailing pattern in canonical-creation-id contexts elsewhere, the fix direction reverses.
title: MdnSendRequest.send keyed by String, not Id — type discipline divergence from on_success_update_email
